title: Tensor pullback preserves appending one tensor factor
statement: Let j:Z→X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], B an arbitrary O_X-module, P=tensorPullback j, β the tensor comparison and p_e the recursive tensor-power pullback comparison [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. For every e≥0, let a_B,e: B^e tensor B → B^(e+1) be (B^e tensor ρ_B inverse) followed by tensorPowAddIso(B,e,1).inv. Then β(B^e,B).inv followed by P(a_B,e) and p_(e+1).hom equals (p_e.hom tensor identity(PB)) followed by a_(PB),e. No closed immersion, ideal, coefficient module, block size, section or invertibility hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 01CD, functorial pullback of tensor products and its associator/unit coherence; Tag 09MS, tensor powers in coherent-equation-ses. The recursive append calculation is the pullback part of step 2 of lem-sc-tensor-ideal-section-coefficient-comparison.

proof.text: Use the proved private pullback_power_add in BoundaryCoefficientDegreeSplit at e and 1. Its base normalization uses pullback_monoidal_unit_comparison. The transported monoidal unit map gives the degree-zero inverse comparison; right unitality identifies the inverse right unitor followed by the degree-one inverse comparison with the pullback of the inverse right unitor. Precompose by the inverse degree-e comparison tensored with the identity. Tensorator naturality and whisker exchange reduce to pullback_power_add; cancel the inverse degree-(e+1) comparison. This works for e=0 and arbitrary B, including the tensor unit.

theorem boundaryPullbackPowIso_append {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    (B : X.Modules) (e : ℕ) :
    (boundaryPullbackTensorIso j (B.tensorPow e) B).inv ≫
        (tensorPullback j).map
          ((B.tensorPow e ◁ (ρ_ B).inv) ≫ (B.tensorPowAddIso e 1).inv) ≫
        (boundaryPullbackPowIso j B (e + 1)).hom =
      (boundaryPullbackPowIso j B e).hom ▷ (tensorPullback j).obj B ≫
        (((tensorPullback j).obj B).tensorPow e ◁ (ρ_ ((tensorPullback j).obj B)).inv) ≫
        (((tensorPullback j).obj B).tensorPowAddIso e 1).inv
